strings.if.title: What is intermittent fasting?
strings.if.what: Intermittent fasting (IF) is an eating pattern that alternates planned periods of eating with periods of little or no caloric intake. It focuses mainly on when you eat rather than prescribing a particular food list.
strings.if.examples: Common approaches include daily time-restricted eating (for example, 16:8), the 5:2 pattern, and alternate-day fasting.
strings.if.benefits: Human trials suggest intermittent fasting can help some adults reduce body weight and waist circumference and may improve blood-glucose control, insulin sensitivity, blood pressure and some blood-lipid markers. Effects are usually modest, vary among people and regimens, and are often similar to continuous calorie restriction when total energy intake and weight loss are comparable.
strings.if.limits: Long-term effects on disease prevention, lifespan, cognitive function and the best fasting schedule remain uncertain. Much of the human evidence is short- to medium-term and is concentrated in adults with overweight, obesity or metabolic risk.
strings.if.safety: Fasting is not suitable for everyone. Seek professional advice before fasting if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, under 18, underweight, have a current or past eating disorder, diabetes or another medical condition, or take medicines that can be affected by meal timing. Stop the fast and seek appropriate care for severe weakness, fainting, confusion, dehydration, persistent vomiting or other concerning symptoms.
strings.if.src1: BMJ 2025 systematic review — 99 randomized trials; intermittent fasting and continuous calorie restriction produced broadly similar weight and cardiometabolic outcomes, with generally small differences between strategies.
strings.if.src2: U.S. National Institute on Aging — overview of intermittent-fasting patterns, potential health effects and uncertainty about long-term outcomes.
strings.if.src3: NIH Research Matters, 2024 — an 8–10 hour eating window produced modest benefits over three months in people with metabolic syndrome; longer studies are needed.
strings.if.src4: NIDDK, 2024 — possible benefits and medication-related safety considerations for people with type 2 diabetes.

strings.science.title: Autophagy & fasting science
strings.science.idle: Autophagy is active at basal levels even when you are not fasting. Human research has not established a universal hour when fasting-induced autophagy “starts.”
strings.science.caution: This indicator is educational, not a measurement of autophagy and not a reason to prolong a fast. Fasting responses vary by tissue, activity, prior diet, glycogen status and other factors.
strings.science.timeline0: 0–8 h — early fast; no clock-based autophagy inference.
strings.science.timeline1: 8–12 h — ketones commonly begin to rise; metabolic switching starts.
strings.science.timeline2: 12–24 h — metabolic transition progresses; autophagy onset in humans remains unproven.
strings.science.timeline3: 24–36 h — human autophagy-related markers have been studied; results are mixed and tissue-dependent.
strings.science.timeline4: 36–48 h — prolonged fasting; a 36 h human muscle study found only modest effects on autophagy mediators.
strings.science.timeline5: 48 h+ — extended fasting; there is no validated whole-body “autophagy level” that can be calculated from elapsed time.
strings.science.stage0t: Autophagy is already active at basal levels. Elapsed fasting time alone cannot show whether it has increased.
strings.science.stage1t: Human ketone levels commonly begin to rise in this window. That metabolic change is not evidence that autophagy has switched on at a specific hour.
strings.science.stage2t: Fuel use shifts further toward fat and ketones, but reviews conclude that a significant fasting-induced rise in human autophagy during an acute fast has not been established.
strings.science.stage3t: Human skeletal-muscle studies at 24–36 hours show mixed or modest changes in autophagy-related markers. Effects differ by tissue and individual context.
strings.science.stage4t: Ketosis generally deepens, but a 36-hour human muscle study found only modest effects on autophagy mediators. There is no validated whole-body autophagy threshold.
strings.science.stage5t: Current human evidence does not let an app calculate an autophagy “level” from fasting duration. Longer fasting should not be interpreted as proportionally more autophagy.
strings.science.src1: Gómez-Virgilio et al., 2022 (PubMed) — autophagy is active at basal levels in cells and responds to nutrient stress.
strings.science.src2: de Cabo & Mattson, NEJM 2019 and 2020 correction — human ketone levels begin rising roughly 8–12 h into fasting and increase further by 48 h.
strings.science.src3: Anton et al., 2022 (PubMed) — review concluding that whether an acute fast produces significant increases in human autophagy remains unknown.
strings.science.src4: Chaudhary et al., 2022 (PubMed) — 12–24 h fasting did not show robust activation of autophagy markers in human skeletal muscle.
strings.science.src5: Dethlefsen et al., 2018 (PubMed) — 36 h fasting produced only modest changes in autophagy-related markers in human skeletal muscle, influenced by training status.

strings.help.title: About & Help
strings.help.installIOS1: Open the app's web address in Safari.
strings.help.installIOS2: Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
strings.help.installIOS3: Keep Open as Web App enabled if iOS shows that option, then tap Add.
strings.help.installAndroid1: Open the app's web address in Chrome or another browser that supports PWA installation.
strings.help.installAndroid2: Open the browser menu and choose Install app or Add to Home screen.
strings.help.installAndroid3: Confirm the installation. Fasting Tracker will appear on the Home screen/app launcher and can work offline after its files are cached.
strings.help.backupText: The app automatically keeps rolling internal JSON snapshots after meaningful changes and reminds you every 7 days to use Back up now for an external JSON copy in Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, or another secure location. Deleted fasting audit records are included in that JSON until you restore or permanently delete them. When enough history exists it keeps 5 recent, 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly recovery points. Internal snapshots are lost if this installation is removed. The JSON file itself is the complete external backup; no companion text file is required. Before reinstalling to change the Home Screen icon, create an external backup; after reinstalling, use Import to restore it.
strings.help.privacyText: Your fasting and weight records stay in this device's local web-app storage. The hosted website contains only the app files and does not receive your fasting or weight history. Each friend who installs the app has separate local data. Clearing browser or website data can remove local records, so keep a recent backup.
strings.help.timeZoneText: Fasts and weight entries remember the time zone in which they were created, so historical clock times and calendar-day charts do not shift if you later travel to another time zone.
strings.help.autophagyText: The science card deliberately does not claim that autophagy starts at a fixed hour. Autophagy occurs continuously at a basal level, and current human studies do not support a universal fasting-duration threshold. The card separates well-established metabolic timing from more uncertain autophagy evidence and links to the studies used.
strings.help.consistencyText: Gamification is optional. A fast that reaches its chosen target earns 10 XP regardless of whether it ends exactly at the target or continues much longer. Weight logging earns 2 XP per distinct calendar day. The system deliberately does not reward extreme fasting duration.
strings.help.versionHelp: Useful when checking which release is installed
